text: Mahlagha Mallah (Persian: مه‌لقا ملاح‎; 21 September 1917 – 8 November 2021) was an Iranian environmental activist and librarian, recognized as the "Mother of Iran's Environment." She was born on 21 September 1917 in a caravanserai near Now Kandeh, while her parents were en route to Mashhad on a pilgrimage. Her mother, Khadijeh Afzal Vaziri, and her grandmother, Bibi Khanoom Astarabadi, were both women's rights activists in Iran. Her father, Aghabzorg Mallah, worked for the government and resided in various cities. At 17, she married Hossein Abolhasani. After studying philosophy, social sciences, and sociology at the University of Tehran, she earned a master's degree in social sciences in 1958. In 1966, she moved to Paris to pursue a PhD at the University of the Sorbonne, which she completed in 1968, and also studied librarianship at the National Library of France. Upon returning to Iran, she worked as a librarian at the Psychology Research Institute Library at the University of Tehran. It was only after her retirement from librarianship in 1977 that she and her husband began environmental campaigning. Her interest in environmental issues was influenced by her mother's activism and deepened when, in 1973, she read a book on pollution to learn how to catalogue it. After retiring, she began researching pollution in Tehran, initially visiting homes and speaking with residents about environmental concerns. In 1993, she founded the Women's Society Against Environmental Pollution, the first non-governmental environmental organization in Iran, which was officially registered with the Ministry of the Interior in 1995. By 2012, it had become the largest environmental group in Iran, with branches in 14 Iranian cities and had enabled over 25,000 families to recycle. In 2011, it was considered the most popular environmental group in the country. In 2009, the society published a report titled "Water Rights," highlighting the urgent need to conserve wetland habitats in Iran, including in the Zayandeh Rud region. Mallah is described as an ecofeminist, emphasizing that women must be central to environmentalism. Her life story was featured in the 2015 documentary All My Trees, directed by Rakhshān Banietemad. She passed away on 8 November 2021, at the age of 104.
